activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of a Span

feedback.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, our matrix is already in a row echelon form.

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}.
$$
